headline: High: shared MCP and broad egress create default leakage and injection pathways; next-ai-draw-io also adds browser/API exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and next-ai-draw-io also uses MCP plus natural-language commands, so a shared instruction channel exists. Haystack’s search-RAG role can ingest external content, and next-ai-draw-io can render or act on AI-assisted inputs. The pair is not proven to auto-bridge, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are connected to the same MCP server or shared workspace
IF next-ai-draw-io passes untrusted document text into Haystack prompts without sanitization
mitigations: Disable shared MCP endpoints between the two agents
Route untrusted content through a plain-text sanitizer before either agent sees it
Require provenance labels on all MCP-fed content
Use separate workspaces for each agent

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and next-ai-draw-io sends data to multiple third-party model APIs while handling PDFs, images, and API keys. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive document contents can flow from B into A or out through B’s cloud calls. The default egress surface makes leakage materially dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same files or mounted workspace
IF next-ai-draw-io is configured to send document text to a hosted model API
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Block outbound internet for Haystack unless explicitly needed
Use local-only models for next-ai-draw-io
Remove API keys from the shared environment
Restrict file permissions to least privilege

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and both use MCP, while next-ai-draw-io also supports multiple instances. That creates overlapping mutable control surfaces and possible race conditions on shared resources, though the profiles do not prove shared filesystem writes or git mutation. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same MCP-backed resource
IF both are launched against the same mutable workspace or API quota
mitigations: Assign separate API keys or quotas
Serialize access to shared MCP resources
Run only one writer at a time
Use per-agent working directories

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG system that can generate retrieved answers, and next-ai-draw-io is designed for natural-language commands and AI-assisted visualization. That makes it plausible for B to treat A’s output as authoritative when producing diagrams or actions. No verification step is documented, so the cascade risk exists in default use but is not proven high.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io consumes Haystack output as source text without human review
IF Haystack outputs are used to populate diagrams or downstream actions
mitigations: Insert a human review step before B acts on A output
Require citations or source links in A outputs
Mark A output as untrusted in B prompts
Use a validation checklist for generated diagrams

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack is documented as touching anonymous usage statistics, while next-ai-draw-io handles PDFs, images, text files, and API keys with broad third-party model routing. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, but they do show different retention-sensitive surfaces and secret handling, so compliance gaps are plausible and should be treated as medium.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through next-ai-draw-io
IF logs or telemetry retain document contents or API keys beyond policy
mitigations: Disable telemetry where possible
Document retention settings for both agents
Keep regulated data out of next-ai-draw-io
Review vendor DPAs and residency settings
Purge API keys from shared logs
